items.q: What defines a star as being on the 'main sequence'?
items.correct: It fuses hydrogen into helium in its core.
items.misconception: It is the largest stage of a star's life.
items.why: Students think main sequence = most spectacular. It's defined by the FUEL: hydrogen fusion. Stars spend most of their lives there because hydrogen is plentiful and fusion is stable.

items.q: What fuel does a main sequence star fuse in its core?
items.why: It's Hydrogen. “Helium” is the classic near-miss here; knowing why it's wrong is worth as much as knowing the right answer.

items.q: What is left behind after a low-mass star sheds a planetary nebula?
items.why: It's White dwarf. “Neutron star” is the classic near-miss here; knowing why it's wrong is worth as much as knowing the right answer.

items.q: Approximately what core temperature is needed in kelvin to start hydrogen fusion?
items.why: The real figure is 10000000. The wrong options cluster deliberately close — anchor the exact number to one concrete fact so it can't drift.
